question.problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{6})=-\frac{1}{2}$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$ If the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is ${x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$

current_example.problem: Consider the equation $-2\sqrt{3}\sin\left(2x+\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) - 3 = 0$ for $0 \leq x \lt 2\pi.$ If the solutions $x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4$ are written in ascending order, what is $x_1\cdot x_4?$
current_example.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

First, we rearrange the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{3})-3 & =0 \\ -2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{3}) & =3 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\frac{3}{-2\sqrt{3}} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{3}) & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{\pi }{3} & =\frac{4\pi }{3}+2n\pi , & \, & \, & 2x+\frac{\pi }{3} & =\frac{5\pi }{3}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =\pi +2n\pi  & \, & \, & 2x & =\frac{4\pi }{3}+2n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{2\pi }{3}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{2n\pi }{2} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{2\pi }{3}+\frac{3n\pi }{3} \\ x & =\frac{(1+2n)\pi }{2} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{\pi (2+3n)}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0, \pm 1, \pm 2,\ldots$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0 \leq x \lt 2\pi.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $x=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}.$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$ and $x=\dfrac{5\pi}{3}.$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0 \leq x \lt 2\pi.$ So, the solutions $x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x = \dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{2\pi}{3},\dfrac{3\pi}{2},\dfrac{5\pi}{3}.
$$

Finally, since $x_1 = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $x_4 = \dfrac{5\pi}{3},$ we have

$$
x_1\cdot x_4 =  \dfrac{\pi}{2} \cdot  \dfrac{5\pi}{3} = \dfrac{5\pi^2}{6}.
$$
